name: Cantonese nationalism
summary: Cantonese nationalism holds that the Cantonese are a distinct people, defined by language, culture and history, who should govern themselves, either through autonomy or independence of Guangdong or the Cantonese-speaking area. Its historical strand (Au Ku-kap, Chen Jiongming) stressed provincial self-rule within a federal China, and its modern expression centres on defending Cantonese against Mandarin promotion and on Hong Kong localism.
scope: A cultural-linguistic strand: Au Ku-kap's 1902 'New Canton' (Guangdong self-rule leading to a federal China), Chen Jiongming's 1920s provincial autonomy, the 2010 Guangzhou Cantonese-language protests, the Guangzhou independence slogans of 2018, and Hong Kong localism as a neighbouring movement. Excludes mainland Chinese nationalism and fully independent Hong Kong separatism as a separate strand. Most economic and social statements are not addressed by this movement.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a Cantonese-nationalist issue; Hong Kong localists and Guangdong autonomists vary on welfare, so no position is inferable.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The sources show no common wage stance; localist groups span left and right on economics.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Au Ku-kap and Chen Jiongming were reformers, and localists are economically mixed, so adherents split.

public-ownership.rationale: Localist and autonomist movements are not socialist; I infer mild disagreement from their liberal-reformist roots.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position; localist camps include both left-liberals and market-oriented figures.

unions-good.rationale: Sources do not address labour; localism includes both pro-labour and pro-business groups.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not addressed by sources; no distinctive stance can be drawn from the identity-based politics.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economics is secondary to identity here, and adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Localists oppose welfare for mainland newcomers but not welfare generally, so no clear answer.

worker-ownership.rationale: No documented stance; not a theme of the movement.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents face state surveillance and security laws, and localists oppose central-government control, so I infer mild distrust.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Unaddressed by the sources; no basis for an answer.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Localists have been condemned as xenophobic and have seen speech restricted by the state, so they tend to resist speech limits; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Localists oppose central pre-screening of leaders and favour deliberative democracy; a strongman bypassing gridlock fits poorly.

state-harmful.rationale: Cantonese nationalists want their own state or autonomous government (Au's Guangdong self-government), not no state.

empower-police-military.rationale: Localists clashed with police and fear central security forces; inferred mild disagreement.

decide-locally.rationale: Au Ku-kap's thesis was 'Guangdong people managing Guangdong affairs' with provinces self-governing first, and localists demand autonomy from the central government.

traditional-family.rationale: Cultural localists keep traditional customs but the movement has no family doctrine; adherents split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; localists are divided on social issues.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is not a feature of the movement and localism is largely secular; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending Cantonese language and culture against Mandarin promotion is the movement's core, as in the 2010 Guangzhou protests.

gradual-change.rationale: Au Ku-kap called for rapid independence efforts and 2018 slogans were radical, though many adherents favour autonomy; inferred mild disagreement.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Localists oppose mainland immigration and visitor influx, though this is the Hong Kong strand and critics call it xenophobic.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; localists seek outside attention but no position on international bodies' power.

free-trade.rationale: Guangdong was a trading region, but the sources record no position on trade.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own nation is Cantonese rather than a state, and the question is ambiguous for it.

open-borders.rationale: Localists resist mainland influx and want control of who enters Hong Kong, so open borders runs against their stance.

revolution-justified.rationale: Au Ku-kap urged secret societies to restore Han land and Guangdong declared independence in 1911; modern adherents also include radical groups, though mild autonomists differ.

experts-over-public.rationale: Localists favour deliberative democracy and distrust elites; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Not a stance of the movement; I infer disagreement from its liberal and market-city setting.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; no documented trade position.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a movement concern; I infer rejection as the movement is not communist.

one-party-rule.rationale: Adherents oppose central one-party control: localists reject pre-screened elections, and 2018 Guangzhou slogans coincided with removal of term limits.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Au Ku-kap attacked the Manchu court as foreign rule and endorsed popular sovereignty; modern adherents are republican or not concerned.

democracy-best.rationale: Localists favour deliberative democracy and Guangzhou activists seek democratic reform, though some localists are militantly sceptical of pan-democrats.

direct-votes.rationale: Localists favour deliberative democracy but no stance on referendums is documented.

workers-councils.rationale: Not a feature of the movement; inferred from its liberal-democratic orientation.

right-to-secede.rationale: Independence advocates claim Cantonese or Hongkongers have a right to self-determination, but milder autonomists seek only autonomy, so only agree.

natural-rulers.rationale: Au Ku-kap's shareholder analogy made the government a hired shopkeeper of the people, which is incompatible with natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Localists include militant and peaceful wings; Guangzhou activists hold the movement to peaceful methods, so adherents split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; I infer mild agreement from the secular character of localism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular character of the movement.

military-superiority.rationale: The nation has no army; adherents are the weaker party against Beijing and the idea is not theirs.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Cantonese nation is defined by language and culture, and Hong Kong localists have a civic Hongkonger identity, yet nativist strands exist; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Not a framework for the movement, which centres on regional identity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Cantonese nationalists claim homeland territory but not as indigeneity in the usual sense.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; some localists look to British rule favourably, others do not.

civilizational-union.rationale: Adherents want a distinct Cantonese nation, not unions by shared civilization; Au Ku-kap wanted provinces first.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Localists defend individual freedoms against central authority; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the commercial and urban character of the Cantonese region.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed directly; adherents face censorship and surveillance, so I infer support for private communication.

restore-past-order.rationale: Some localists look back to British Hong Kong and Au Ku-kap looked forward to a new China; split.

direct-action.rationale: Localists favour militant protest, but the movement also uses elections and petitions; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in the movement suggests it; inferred rejection.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; inferred rejection as the movement is not communist.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's non-Marxist character.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Not addressed; inferred strong rejection of dictatorship from democratic localism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's non-Marxist character.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; localists favour civil liberties against central restriction, so inferred mild agreement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement claims collective rights of a language group and region, so it is unlikely to say rights belong only to individuals.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagreement since the movement stands apart from the central army.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Localists insist on political voice and autonomy rather than leaving; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; the movement defines identity by language and culture, not race.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favour democratic representation.

total-state.rationale: Adherents resist state-directed culture, as in the 2010 and 2018 episodes, so a state directing all life runs against their stance.

national-rebirth.rationale: Cantonese nationalists speak of preserving rather than being reborn; the question does not fit well.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Aims are to hold a Guangdong or Cantonese-speaking area; expansion is not on the agenda.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Au Ku-kap's contract-of-the-people language is opposed to personal oaths of loyalty.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; overseas Cantonese protest abroad but no right of return is documented.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cantonese is not extinct, but the movement wants it kept in state, schooling and media; I infer mild agreement, with the premise partly mismatched.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed directly; no documented position.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; localists emphasise institutions and rights over rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Cantonese nationalism holds the Cantonese are a distinct nation that should have an independent or autonomous homeland; Hong Kong localists claim self-determination.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Localists oppose benefit tourism and mainland newcomers drawing on Hong Kong welfare; inferred from that campaign.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Protecting Cantonese language and cultural heritage is central, so sacrificing inherited institutions for progress is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; some localists seek Western support, others do not.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is organised by region and language, not by class.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; commercial Cantonese centres suggest rejection.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; localists are criticised for xenophobia but do not advocate racial law; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed; the movement sees the state as a tool of central power, not class.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Adherents resist assimilation to Mandarin-speaking norms, though localists want newcomers to adapt to Hong Kong; I take mild disagreement for assimilation into a Chinese national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some nativist localists speak of mainland population influx as a deliberate dilution, but this is not mainstream; split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Localists distrust pan-democrats and the central-government establishment, so mild agreement is inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; localists criticise police conduct, so mild agreement is inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred strong rejection since Cantonese identity is cultural and linguistic.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not addressed directly; I infer mild agreement from democratic localism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; some radical localists call mainland migration colonisation but the statement is about settler states generally.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Au Ku-kap said the people are shareholders who can replace their hired government, and localists demand autonomy and democratic choice of the Chief Executive.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; localist hostility to mainland migrants does not extend to forced transfer, and adherents would reject it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on militancy.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Hong Kong authorities banned the Hong Kong National Party, which adherents opposed; inferred disagreement.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed in these terms; the localist complaint of central domination fits it, so mild agreement.

separated-powers.rationale: Au Ku-kap drew on German and American federalism with provinces self-governing under a national government, favouring divided power.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nativist localists say so of mainland influx, but cultural localists do not; split.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Adherents face suspensions of protections under security law, so I infer strong disagreement.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 2010 protests were against official pressure on Cantonese broadcasting and censorship followed, so government control of media is opposed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Localists want tighter control of mainland inflow and residence, so a long wait is inferred as mildly favoured.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Au Ku-kap wanted provinces to unite in a federal structure, but modern adherents have no EU-like stance; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from preference for parliamentary or federal arrangements.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adherents resist state control of culture and language; inferred mild disagreement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Slogans in Guangzhou appeared as term limits for Xi were removed, so adherents disliked unlimited tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; mild agreement is inferred from participatory localism.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Cantonese identity centres on Guangzhou and Hong Kong, which are cities; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Cantonese nationalists in part want Guangdong and Hong Kong cooperation across the border, but there is no documented stance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Protesters said Mandarin and Cantonese should coexist and the mother tongue not be given up, implying cultural equality over hierarchy.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Localists dispute birth tourism; not a documented stance on descent versus birth.

minority-language-support.rationale: The movement exists to defend Cantonese against Mandarin promotion; Hong Kong localists defend Cantonese and its writing, and Guangzhou rallies demanded keeping it in local TV.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Au Ku-kap's independence was political, with no property change demanded; inferred disagreement.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; mild agreement is inferred from autonomy and self-determination demands.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Adherents defend freedoms against central control; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Localists oppose pre-screening of Chief Executive candidates but not specifically direct head-of-state elections.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Radical localists see Hong Kong rule by Beijing as illegitimate, but the statement is general; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents face Beijing's suppression of independence talk and reject force against separatist movements; Guangdong's 1911 secession and 1922 Chen Jiongming rebellion were crushed by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy within China with a distinct legal and economic order is the milder localist demand and the Chen Jiongming provincial-constitution model.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Au Ku-kap treated rulers as hired by the people, which excludes sacred rulers.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Au Ku-kap's contract view and the localist demand for constitutional autonomy are opposed to a ruler above the law.

leader-cult.rationale: The 2018 Guangzhou slogans were a reaction to term-limit removal for Xi, and localists oppose centralised personal rule.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Cantonese-speaking area claims exist, but these are claims to a homeland, not by a state over foreign territory; no stance.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cantonese nationalism separates Cantonese from the broader Han and Mandarin polity, so union among kin peoples is not its aim.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Protests and localism demand self-governed cultural and educational space for Cantonese within China, including keeping Cantonese in school and media.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; localists defend rule-of-law constraints; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; Guangdong and Hong Kong are trade regions; inferred disagreement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not addressed; most adherents are non-violent in practice.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Au Ku-kap attacked Manchu hereditary rule; mild agreement inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Localists want local history and identity taught, and the Education Bureau Cantonese controversy suggests concern for local curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Adherents reject rule by a more 'advanced' centre; Cantonese are said to be dominated by Beijing.

patriotic-education.rationale: Localists oppose national education campaigns in Hong Kong promoting Chinese identity; inferred mild disagreement.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; adherents see Beijing's influence as unwanted.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; Cantonese regions are export-oriented.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Localists defend Basic Law protections; mild agreement inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Au Ku-kap called people shareholders choosing their government, and localists demand elections without pre-screening.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Au Ku-kap said the people could replace a government that fails them, and localists back resistance to central overreach.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is political; inferred strong rejection.

native-born-offices.rationale: Localist nativism favours local-born holders of local office; inferred from that tendency.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; localists oppose communist-party rule, so mild agreement is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Beijing says this to justify non-democracy and localists oppose it; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust central military power.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; traditional customs are kept by cultural localists but no doctrine.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagreement from market-city setting.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; mild agreement is inferred from democratic autonomy claims.

single-official-language.rationale: Adherents oppose making Mandarin the sole common language: Guangzhou protesters wanted Cantonese kept on TV alongside Mandarin and localists defend Cantonese in public life.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; localists oppose mainland buyers but not foreigners generally.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are subjects of such pressure and reject it.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Hong Kong authorities cite foreign funding to restrict activism; adherents oppose, inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Localists oppose mainland buying and parallel trading; mild agreement inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek foreign attention but oppose Beijing's interference.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed directly; protest against censorship supports mild agreement.

informal-organisation.rationale: Localist and Guangzhou activism uses small informal groups but no doctrine is stated.

religious-nation.rationale: Cantonese identity is linguistic and cultural, not religious; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Adherents resist deference to Beijing's authority over Guangdong and Hong Kong.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Au Ku-kap's Guangdong self-rule implies managing its own revenue, though sources do not state it.

defeat-communism.rationale: Localists oppose Communist Party rule but no stance on global struggle is documented.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Cantonese writing defense concerns Mandarin norms, but there is no documented stance on foreign loanwords, which Cantonese freely uses.

majority-settlement.rationale: Localists oppose mainland settlement in Hong Kong; encouraging majority settlement in minority regions is the opposite of their stance.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Cantonese nationalists base claims on Guangdong's provincial borders, but the sources do not take a general stance.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Adherents are themselves the opposition suppressed by the state; they strongly reject it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Adherents complain of Beijing exploiting Guangdong and Hong Kong, so the reverse is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Localists favour deliberative democracy and active popular participation.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Localists reject both pan-democrat and establishment frames and organise by identity; inferred mild agreement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Au Ku-kap's people-as-shareholders view locates authority in the people, not God.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views on the West and China.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Au Ku-kap attacked dynastic rule and localists demand open elections.

property-franchise.rationale: Localists demand wider, genuine democracy; a property franchise contradicts it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not addressed; localists defend rule of law against arbitrary central power, so mild agreement inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Localists define belonging by culture and residence and demand democracy, so racial franchise is rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; localist movements organise online, so mild agreement is inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed directly; criticism of censorship supports mild agreement.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Localists boycott mainland-linked shops, but that is not a religious minority; inferred disagreement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Localists favour deliberative democracy, so mild agreement is inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; mild agreement is inferred from preference for autonomy and consultation.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed generally; the Guangzhou slogans coincided with abolition of Xi's term limits, implying mild support.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Localist nativism opposes extending political rights to newcomers; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the modern movement is nonviolent protest, but nothing in its sources commits it to absolute pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its definition of the Cantonese as a distinct people with their own language, culture and history, which implies long continuity; the sources do not state a claim about antiquity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred that a language-and-culture movement takes the conventional view.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no position documented, inferred from its focus on a unified people.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: the movement is expressed through civic protest and language defence, without a documented cult of national martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Its politics concern language rights and self-rule (Au Ku-kap's federalism, the 2010 protests), framed as civic claims, not a spiritual war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: Cantonese live widely overseas and the movement defends a language and culture rather than gathering the people in one place.

culture-before-state.rationale: The best-known modern action, the 2010 protests, defended language and culture, and autonomy is sought within a federal China; inferred that cultural defence is the priority.

god-not-male.rationale: Religion is not a theme in the sources and adherents have no recorded position.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religion is not a theme in the sources and adherents have no recorded position.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: Cantonese claims are about language and self-rule, and Hong Kong localism's concerns are not documented as a demand that business be reserved for the majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the aim of autonomy for the whole Cantonese-speaking area, which spans several administrative units.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

second-chamber.rationale: Au Ku-kap's New Canton envisioned a federal China, and federal systems usually give the provinces a second chamber; inferred, not stated.

municipal-property.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Au Ku-kap and Chen Jiongming favoured provincial self-rule within a federation, but confederal town assemblies are not part of it.

family-wage.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from localist and Guangzhou activism under censorship, where anonymity protects dissenters.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from Hong Kong localism's liberal and rights-based concerns against state pressure on Cantonese.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Au Ku-kap and Chen Jiongming sought provincial self-rule as a right within a federal China, not a grant the centre could withdraw.

gm-crops.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Cantonese are defined by language, culture and history, not race; inferred from that cultural basis.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Cantonese language and ancestry drives the Cantonese-rights protests, though the pride is cultural rather than racial.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from a movement of autonomy and language defence that has no military programme.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The movement defines the Cantonese as a distinct people by language, culture and history, and rejects their inclusion in a Mandarin-based nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from Hong Kong localism's focus on democratic territorial self-rule; religious electorates are not part of the movement.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The partition-plot claim belongs to Chinese state nationalism; Cantonese nationalists instead resist central control, so they would not endorse it.

free-public-college.rationale: Not a Cantonese-nationalist issue; the sources show no common tuition stance.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; localist groups span left and right on economics and environment.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on preserving Cantonese culture and the homeland for later generations; not stated directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources show no position on gender; localists vary.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no position is inferable.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Au Ku-kap argued for popular sovereignty over government, but did not address treaty secrecy; no position is inferable.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed; autonomists differ on economic policy and capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: a movement seeking autonomy through civic and cultural protest, not armed groups, would accept the usual state monopoly on force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the sources never address conscript refusal; adherents are plausibly split between pacifist and self-defence views.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The movement does not address labour relations; its focus is language and self-rule.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied economic views.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed, though Guangdong-versus-centre revenue grievances give no clear direction on borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is regional and cultural, not about the global economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: Au Ku-kap and Chen Jiongming sought a federal reordering of China, not the destruction of the state machinery as such.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the provincial self-rule tradition (federalism, 'decide locally'): a self-governing Guangdong would be free to choose its own arrangements.

sacred-nation.rationale: Cantonese nationalism is defined by language and culture and a distinct people, but the sources give no sacralised view of the nation; it is also mostly secular.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed by this movement; no position can be inferred from its principles.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The movement's core grievance is that the Mandarin-speaking centre suppresses Cantonese language and culture, and the Guangdong revenue and Hong Kong localist framing treat the centre as extracting from and ruling the periphery like a colonial power.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; no sourced position on human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the 2010 protests over Guangzhou TV's Cantonese-language programming, which show adherents want publicly provided Cantonese media, though independence from government is not discussed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not a topic of the movement; its sources show it concerned with language, autonomy and identity rather than religious doctrine.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural policy is not addressed in the sources; the movement's concerns are linguistic and political, so no lean can be inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear arms are never addressed by a movement for Guangdong self-rule or Hong Kong localism; no inference is possible.

workers-own-party.rationale: The sources record no position on class parties; Au Ku-kap's concern was provincial self-rule and popular sovereignty, not class representation.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the liberal, rights-minded localist outlook documented for Hong Kong localism; the issue itself is not discussed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the modern, liberal localist outlook and Au Ku-kap's popular-sovereignty reasoning; equal inheritance is not discussed in the sources.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Activists insist Cantonese is a language in its own right, distinct from Mandarin, as in the 2010 protests; inferred, since the sources do not address regional naming directly.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Pollution liability is not addressed by the movement, and the sources give nothing to infer a lean from.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Au Ku-kap grounded government in popular sovereignty, with the people as shareholders who may replace it, which suggests no formal role for hereditary or customary leaders; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The movement does not address environmental policy, and its sources offer nothing to infer a position from.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Hong Kong localism is tied to defending rule of law and judicial independence against central control, so fixed sentences are likely disfavoured; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Localists defend Cantonese against Mandarin and press immigrants to adapt to local identity, so requiring the local language is a likely lean; inferred from the localism source.

notes: Adherents split between autonomy within China and outright independence; most economic and social statements are inferred at low confidence because the movement is identity-driven.
